context:
Earlier waves ported and audited core (VirgaCore), network (VirgaNetwork), repo (VirgaRepo), posting-text and timers (VirgaPosting), the insights tables (VirgaInsights), the Defense engine (VirgaDefense) and the demo world (VirgaDemo); the theme, session (VirgaSession) and the archive (VirgaArchive) are ported and audited too (notes/session.md, notes/archive.md). ios/STATUS.md says where the port stands.

Each domain's API map, conventions and known gaps are in ios/porting/notes/<domain>.md (core, network, repo, posting-text, timers, insights, defense, demo-world, theme, session, archive). Before writing code, read the notes for every target you build on: they name the types and functions to reuse (JSCompat, JSONValue, AppLocale, JSDate, HTTPTransport and MockTransport, XRPCAgent, VirgaBackend, KeyValueStore and FileStore, Locked, and so on). Never define a second copy of a type another target owns.

ios/porting/WEB-BUGS.md lists the web bugs already found (the Swift port keeps the web's behaviour, bug included, unless the notes say otherwise). Report new ones in your result; don't fix web code.

Known harness flaw: the fixture writer's toJSON in ios/parity/cases/_helpers.js assigns keys with out[k] =, so a __proto__ key is lost, and it recurses, so a value nested ~2,000 deep reads as a thrown error. Keep generators away from both.

Another chain works concurrently in a second worktree on other domains (listed in your brief). Stay inside the files your brief names; where you need something from a domain the other chain is porting, take it as an injected closure or protocol in your own target and say so in your result, so the merge can wire it.

demo-network: harness/fakeServer.js (session, terms and proxy routes only)

chainA.brief:
Port the rest of the web harness's network into VirgaDemo, so the iOS app's demo mode, its SwiftUI previews and its UI tests run against the same made-up world the web harness shows, through the app's real code paths. The harness isn't in ios/parity/modules/ (that map covers src/ only): record each file in ios/VirgaKit/Sources/VirgaDemo/README.md's table instead (status, Swift files, fixtures, synced = `sha256sum harness/<file> | cut -c1-12`), and give every Swift file a `// Ports harness/<file>` header. Read ios/porting/notes/demo-world.md and that README first: DemoWorld, the worlds, Repo, Views, Crowd, BuildCar and PNG are ported already.

What to build:
1. **harness/fakeXrpc.js** (the signed-in agent): its methods answered from DemoWorld and written back to it (records, blobs, drafts, preferences, bookmarks), its checks (writing another repo, create over an existing record, a swap that doesn't match, a call the granted scope doesn't cover, with the PDS's wording), scopesFor, mintServiceToken/readServiceToken, DRAFT_LIMIT. In Swift this is an XRPC answerer by NSID that VirgaNetwork's XRPC client can be pointed at.
2. **harness/fakeNetwork.js** (createRouter): every host the app reads, routed to the world: the public AppView, the PLC directory, the accounts' PDS (listRecords, getRecord, getRepo's CAR via DemoWorld.repoCar, blobs), Constellation, Bluesky's card and video services; anything else refused loudly. As a VirgaNetwork `HTTPTransport` (`DemoTransport`) over a DemoWorld, with the harness's latency option.
3. **Virga's server, the part the session needs** (from harness/fakeServer.js): /api/oauth/session, /api/oauth/logout, /api/terms/status and /api/terms/accept, and /api/oauth/proxy and /api/oauth/upload-blob forwarding to the fake agent as the account named by the token (read how VirgaSession's SessionController.backendAgent and VirgaNetwork's BackendClient send signed-in XRPC through the proxy, and answer in that shape). Every other /api/* route answers as fakeServer.js answers a route it doesn't know, or with a clearly worded 503 for the routes a later port will add (scheduling, timers, the adviser, Defense), and the README says which.
4. **harness/fakeSession.jsx** (the demo session): `DemoSession`, which builds a VirgaSession SessionModel over SessionController with NoBrowserSessions, in-memory key-value and secret stores, and DemoTransport, with Mira and Field Lab signed in as long sessions (tokens minted by the fake server), and the harness flags that apply as a `DemoOptions` struct: accounts=1, mode (long sessions only on iOS; say so), signedout, expired=<handle>, scope=read, defense, terms=ask|down, latency, now. Port harness.js's readFlags for those flags too (so a launch argument string can be read the same way), and createHarness's parts that remain.
5. Tests: parity where it is pure (scopesFor, the service tokens, readFlags; the router's answers to a list of requests, recorded by a generator that runs the web router with `createRouter` over the harness's worlds at a fixed now, and replayed against DemoTransport in Swift); port harness/fakeXrpc.test.js and the parts of fakeServer.test.js that cover the routes you port; and one end-to-end test: VirgaArchive's ArchiveModel first build for Mira over DemoTransport completes, and its counts (posts, followers, follows, notifications, blocks, lists) are what the world holds.

Keep fixtures under ~1 MB each (record counts and hashes for big answers, as the demo-world fixtures do). Stay inside VirgaDemo and its tests (and the smallest addition to VirgaNetwork or VirgaSession if one is truly needed, tested, and said in your result). Two other chains are working concurrently in other worktrees: one is auditing Defense and then porting the templates (VirgaDefense, VirgaPosting/Templates), the other is porting the rest of insights (VirgaInsights). fakeDefense.js and the rest of fakeServer.js (scheduling, timers, AI, Defense) are a later step; leave them pending in the README.
